text:
support-alex: Customer reported intermittent invalid JSON from /v1/generate when json_mode=true. They copied one response that looks like two objects stitched together.

support-alex: Customer response example:
```
{"session":"s-789","output":{"items":[{"id":"a1","text":"{\"name\":\"Zoe\""}],"extra":{"id":"b1","text":"{\"name\":\"Max\"}"}}}
```

carla-sre: That looks like object boundary bleed. Any request_id, model, pool? 

support-alex: Provided: request_id=req_20260402_9012, model=redwood-large-v1, pool=dedicated-eu-west-2, client was sending ~280 rps. They enabled prefix_cache for repeated system prompts.

deploy-bot: Noted: runtime v2.14.2 deployed to ded-eu-west-2 at 2026-04-02T11:05Z.

jun-runtime: Suspect batching + prefix cache buffer reuse. If two batched responses share a scratch buffer and a prefix flush happens mid-assemble, fragments can join. We haven't seen this exact shape before.

maya-ux: Customer says problem started when they flipped structured JSON + increased concurrency. They can reproduce by hitting the same prefix key concurrently.

support-alex: Server logs for req_20260402_9012 (trimmed):
```
[11:06:08.221] batch=b_2327 shard=s5
[11:06:08.223] kv: prefix fetch key=p:org:sys -> hit
[11:06:08.224] assemble start req=req_20260402_9012
[11:06:08.225] assemble start req=req_20260402_9013
[11:06:08.226] error: json_boundary_mismatch: expected '}' but found '{'
[11:06:08.227] write_chunk req=req_20260402_9012 off=0 len=640
[11:06:08.228] write_chunk req=req_20260402_9013 off=0 len=612
```

jun-runtime: Adjacent writes with same offsets are the smoking gun. Repro plan: two concurrent POSTs with same prefix_cache_key and json_mode=true; throttle to force batching window to combine. I ran a local stress and reproduced merged JSON blobs.

omar-cs: Customer impact: their parser returns 502 on invalid JSON, causing cascading failures in their service for ~25 minutes. They retried and incurred additional charges.

support-alex: Temporary mitigation given: set prefix_cache_enabled=false and reduce max_concurrency to <100. They confirmed corruption stopped after those changes.

jun-runtime: Immediate patch: avoid reusing shared assembly buffers across requests; allocate per-request buffer in critical path. Performance hit small on tail; will backport to v2.14.4 and canary tomorrow.

carla-sre: Creating incident INC-2026-112. Add repro script, request ids, and customer contact. Set severity=P1.

billing-bot: Flagged potential overcharge for customer due to retries. Billing team to review and propose credit.

jun-runtime: I'll open PR with fencing and unit test that simulates concurrent prefix flush: github.com/redwood/eng-runtime/pull/861

support-alex: Customer accepted workaround and asked for ETA. Told them canary deploy expected in 24-36 hours, full roll in 48-72 hours pending canary results.

carla-sre: Add nightly smoke test to run concurrent-prefix-write pattern against dedicated pools to detect regressions. :eyes:

support-alex: Closing thread for now. Will follow up when patch ships and after billing resolution. :white_check_mark:
